text: Most real loops follow a handful of timeless patterns — learn these and you'll recognize them everywhere.
The accumulator pattern starts with a running total and adds to it each pass through the loop.
[chuckle] The search pattern uses a flag — a boolean that starts false and flips true when you find what you want.
And break bails out early the moment the match is found, so you don't waste time searching further.
[sniff] Python has a special for-else that trips people up — the else runs only if the loop finished without a break.
So if no even number is found, the else block declares them all odd.
[sigh] The collector pattern builds a fresh list, appending one result at a time as you loop.
You'll often replace this exact pattern later with a comprehension, but it's vital to understand the long form first.
[groan] Accumulate, search, flag, collect — spot these four patterns and most loops suddenly look familiar.
